payload.text: A structural mismatch is asserted before any pixel comparison, and fails without reporting a pixel number at all. GRADED ON A SPLIT, snorkeltoast's own framing after they corrected themselves upward: the DETECTOR is red-proved on the real artifact in the run behind FLOORS.md -- cmd_redproof assertion 2 removes a slide from the payload and requires compare_structure to fail, observed in redproof2.log at "PASS: 79 structural difference(s) reported, first: slide COUNT differs: reference 22, new 21". THE CALLER'S ORDERING IS INSPECTION ONLY and redproof is candid about it in its own output, which asserts the ordering by pointing at cmd_compare's STRUCTURE block rather than observing cmd_compare refuse. So the mechanism that finds a mismatch has been made to fire against a real injury; the mechanism that guarantees no pixel number is printed first has been read, not run. THE ROW'S WORD "ids" IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN FAILED: slides carry no id -- collect_segment does not put a segment's `id:` into the payload -- and identity is position plus every rendering parameter except pixels, which is strictly STRONGER than an id would give. The absence is not a gap and must not be read as one. Discharged when cmd_compare's die-before-any-pixel-number is observed rather than inspected.
